lore.basajaun: a huge, hairy guardian of the woods and the flocks. Shepherds said he shouted from the mountains to warn them before a storm, and wolves kept away from flocks he watched. In a famous tale, the clever San Martín Txiki tricked the basajaunak into giving up the secrets of growing wheat and making the saw.
fighter.lamia.name: Lamia
lore.lamia: lamiak lived in rivers and springs. They looked like beautiful women with webbed duck or goose feet and combed their hair with golden combs. Many legends say lamiak built bridges or churches in a single night, but had to stop when the rooster crowed at dawn, leaving one stone forever missing.
fighter.tartalo.name: Tartalo
lore.tartalo: a one-eyed giant shepherd of the mountains who ate people. A captive blinded him with a red-hot roasting spit and escaped among the sheep. Tartalo gave him a magic ring that kept shouting where he was, and he only got free by cutting off his finger. The tale closely mirrors Polyphemus in Homer's *Odyssey*, a great talking point about how stories travel.
lore.galtzagorri: galtzagorriak ("red trousers") are tiny helpers kept in a needle case. They do any job in moments, but instantly demand more work, asking "What do we do?" over and over. Owners struggled to get rid of them; in some tellings the trick was giving them an impossible task.
fighter.gaueko.name: Gaueko
lore.gaueko: an invisible being of the night, sometimes felt as a wind or seen as a dark animal. He punished people who stayed out or kept working after dark, following the saying that the day belongs to day-folk and the night to night-folk.
fighter.akerbeltz.name: Akerbeltz
lore.akerbeltz: farmers kept a black billy goat in the stable in the belief that it protected the animals from disease. Some folklorists link the goat to the word *akelarre* ("goat's meadow"), the name later given to supposed witches' gatherings, which is how a protector ended up cast as a devil in the witch trials.
fighter.herensuge.name: Herensuge
lore.herensuge: the dragon of Basque legend, often with seven heads, lived in caves and demanded tribute from nearby villages. Navarra's best-known version is the dragon of the Aralar legend; that story belongs to a living sanctuary, so the game mentions it in lore but never stages it.
fighter.olentzero.name: Olentzero
lore.olentzero: a charcoal burner from the mountains who comes down on Christmas Eve, a tradition especially strong in Lesaka and the Bortziriak area of Navarra. In one version he was the only jentil who stayed when the giants vanished. He fights as a gentle, smiling boss, and his victory pose is handing out chestnuts.

fighter.aatxe.name: Aatxe
fighter.aatxe.epithet: The red bull of the caves
lore.aatxe: Aatxe ("young bull") is a red bull spirit who lives in caves. On stormy nights he comes out to keep people at home and out of danger, and he chases wrongdoers. Sometimes he takes the shape of a young man.
passive.thickHide.name: Thick hide
fighter.ziripot.name: Ziripot & Zaldiko
lore.ziripot: Ziripot is a character of the carnival of Lantz in Navarre: a big, clumsy man stuffed with sacks of hay who can hardly walk. During the carnival Zaldiko, a man dressed as a little horse, keeps knocking him over, and the crowd helps him up again. The carnival ends when a giant straw figure of the bandit Miel Otxin is burned.
passive.padded.name: Padded
passive.padded.text: Stuffed with hay: takes 15% less damage.
fighter.eate.name: Eate
lore.eate: Eate (also called Egata) is the spirit of storms. Wind, hail and fire from the sky come with him, and floods follow where he passes. People in the valleys watched the sky and hurried home when they felt him coming.
passive.stormBorn.name: Storm-born
fighter.basandere.name: Basandere
lore.basandere: Basandere is the wild woman of the woods, the companion of Basajaun. Like him she knows every path, spring and cave of the forest. In some tales she is seen at the mouth of a cave, combing her long hair.

arena.olite.fact: The fairy-tale palace of Carlos III the Noble, built in the early 1400s, with towers, gardens and once even a menagerie.
arena.irati.fact: One of Europe's largest beech and fir forests. Loggers once floated timber downriver on rafts called almadías.
arena.bidasoa.fact: The Bidasoa runs from Baztan to the sea and forms part of the border with France. Many river legends of lamiak come from this area.
arena.bardenas.fact: A semi-desert of eroded clay towers like Castildetierra, now a UNESCO biosphere reserve. Shepherds still bring their flocks down from the Pyrenees for winter.
arena.urbasa.fact: The Urbasa-Andia plateau holds many dolmens, the stones legend credits to the jentilak, and the turquoise springs of the Urederra.
arena.roncesvalles.fact: In 778 Basque fighters ambushed Charlemagne's rearguard here, the event behind the Song of Roland.
